chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqda told us, saying: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: 'Ubays ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Jabla, from Abu Khalid al-Makfuuf, from some of his companions, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

He, who claims this matter (imamate) in secret, must bring proof for it in public. I asked: And what is this proof that is brought in public? He said: He permits what Allah has permitted and prohibits what Allah has prohibited, and his outward appearance confirms his inward reality.
ai.seo_question: What is the proof of an Imam's authority according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of the era of minor occultation and the rise of pretenders, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that secret claims to the Imamate require public verification through adherence to Sharia. This hadith emphasizes that true authority is evidenced not by esoteric knowledge alone, but by the alignment of outward practice (halal/haram) with inward spiritual integrity, a key criterion in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing authentic Imams from false claimants.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (7) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed bin Oqda narrated from al-Qassim bin Muhammad bin al-Hasan bin Hazim from Obayss bin Hisham from Abu Khalid al-Makfoof from some of his companions that Imam as-Sadiq (as) had said:

“He, who pretends this thing (being an imam) secretly, has to show the evidence openly.” The narrator asked: “What evidence that is to be shown openly?” He said: “To permit what Allah has permitted, to prohibit what Allah has prohibited and to be truthful apparently and internally.”
